threads.thread_goal: Align on program charter, scope, and success criteria for the pilot.

messages.text: Morning all, thanks for joining this channel for the outreach pilot. I have shared a draft of the Community Outreach Program Charter in A1, which should also close most of T1. It outlines objectives, scope, target groups, and some initial success criteria. Given the 21-day window, I would like us to use this thread to stress-test the scope and confirm what we will measure, so that T5 can build on a stable baseline. Please take a look at A1 today and share any concerns about the proposed focus on vulnerable residents in the three priority neighbourhoods, and whether the listed success indicators feel realistic with our current resources.

Thanks for sharing A1. From an HR and volunteer side, the scope around vulnerable residents in the three neighbourhoods makes sense to me, especially given our limited staffing. One question: in A1 we mention both home visits and small group events during the pilot. For staffing planning in T2 and onboarding in T8, it would help if we could clarify whether home visits are definitely in scope for the first 21 days, or if we start only with group events in community spaces.

I have gone through A1 as well. For T3 and T9, starting with three outreach events in community centres feels doable, but adding home visits in the same 21-day period might stretch us, especially with volunteers still learning the ropes. Could we treat home visits as a later phase, after we see how the first events go and once we have the operating procedures in A3 fully tested?

From a coordination angle on T11, I agree with focusing the pilot on centre-based activities first. It keeps the operational risk lower while we are still finalising SOPs in A3 and the knowledge hub structure in A8. We can still include home visits in the longer-term vision in A1, but mark them as out of scope for the initial 21 days.

On the success criteria in A1, I see we have a mix of participation numbers, satisfaction, and some qualitative stories. For T5, it would help if we narrow down to a small set of core indicators that we can realistically capture with existing tools. For example: number of attendees per event, proportion of attendees from the target neighbourhoods, and a simple satisfaction rating collected on paper forms. Anything more complex might be hard to do consistently in the first three events.

Looking at A1 from a communications angle, the focus on the three neighbourhoods is clear, but the description of the target community segments might be a bit broad for promotion planning in A6 and T7. Do we want to prioritise families with children, older adults, or keep it open to all residents who feel vulnerable? This will influence how we frame the key messages and which channels we use.

Good point on the segments. Given our existing relationships and the risks listed in A1, I suggest we prioritise two groups for the pilot: older adults living alone and low-income families with children in those three neighbourhoods. Others can still attend, but our outreach and messaging in A6 and T7 would be tailored to those two groups. Does anyone see major issues with that focus, especially in terms of safeguarding and training content in A5?

From the HR and safeguarding side, focusing on older adults living alone and low-income families is workable. For T8 and A5, we can emphasise boundaries, privacy, and how to respond if volunteers notice signs of neglect or distress in those groups. I do not see extra legal constraints beyond what we already follow, as long as we keep data collection minimal and anonymised where possible.

For the events in T3 and T9, that focus also helps with programming. We can design activities that are friendly for both older adults and families, like information corners plus simple activities for children. It will also make it easier to brief volunteers on what to expect on the day using A3 and A5.

On the metrics, I like the three you suggested. To make sure T10 is manageable, I propose we define the top three success metrics for the pilot as: 1) total number of unique attendees across the first three events, 2) share of attendees from the three target neighbourhoods, and 3) proportion of attendees who report that the event was helpful or very helpful on a short feedback form. We can still collect stories, but those would be for qualitative reporting rather than core KPIs in A4.

Those three metrics are also easy to integrate into our event checklists and the knowledge hub index in A8. We can add a simple section in A3 and A7 so that whoever is leading the event remembers to capture attendance, neighbourhood, and the quick feedback form.

From a communications perspective, those metrics are also easy to explain in the internal briefing linked to T12. We can say we are testing whether we can reach residents in the three neighbourhoods and whether they find the events useful, without overpromising on long-term impact yet.

On the question of home visits: given the time and staffing constraints, I agree with the suggestion to keep them out of scope for the initial 21 days. We can still describe them in A1 as a potential next phase, but for this pilot we will focus on three centre-based events only. That should also reduce safeguarding complexity while we are still refining A3 and A5.

Thanks for clarifying. I will reflect that scope in the staffing and recruitment plan in A2 under T2, so that we recruit and brief volunteers specifically for centre-based events with those two priority groups, not for home visits yet.

If everyone is comfortable, I will update A4 under T5 so that the three metrics we discussed become the top-level indicators for the pilot. We can still list a few optional learning indicators, but they will not be required for every event.

Agreed. To summarise for this thread: for the pilot scope in A1, we will focus on three centre-based events in the three priority neighbourhoods, targeting primarily older adults living alone and low-income families with children. Home visits are described as a future phase but not part of this 21-day pilot. For success metrics, we will track: total unique attendees across the three events, share of attendees from the target neighbourhoods, and proportion of attendees who report the event as helpful or very helpful. These will feed into A4 and T5. Unless there are strong objections today, let us treat this as our confirmed direction so that downstream tasks can proceed.

Thanks for the recap. I will reflect these decisions in the overall timeline under T11 and in the internal briefing for T12, so that leadership and other teams are aligned on the scope and the three core metrics.

threads.thread_goal: Define staffing, volunteer needs, and onboarding approach.

messages.text: Hi all, following the scope decisions in A1, I have uploaded a first draft of the Staffing and Volunteer Recruitment Plan in A2, covering most of T2. It outlines proposed roles for the three centre-based events, estimated time commitments, and a draft recruitment timeline. I have also sketched an onboarding and training flow that we can turn into A5 under T8. In short, I am assuming we need event leads, welcome desk volunteers, activity facilitators, and a data capture helper for each event. Please review A2 and share if the numbers and role descriptions feel realistic.

Thanks for pulling this together. Looking at A2 from the event side for T3 and T9, I see you propose 1 event lead, 2 welcome desk volunteers, 2 activity facilitators, and 1 data helper per event. For the first event, I am a bit worried that 2 activity facilitators might be tight if we have both a quiet space for older adults and a small corner for children. Could we plan for 3 activity facilitators for event 1, even if we scale back later once we see actual attendance?

From a coordination and budget perspective, adding one more activity facilitator for the first event seems manageable, as long as we are clear in A2 that this is a stretch target and that we can run with 2 if recruitment is slower. It might also help with risk management in A3, since we will have more eyes on the room.

On the data helper role: for T10 and A4, it is important that whoever does this is comfortable with basic counting and simple forms. In A2, could we add a short note that data helpers should be either staff or more experienced volunteers, not first-timers, so that we reduce the risk of missing data for our three core metrics?

For the onboarding flow in A5, I see you propose a short online briefing plus an in-person huddle before each event. From a communications angle and thinking about T7, could we also include a simple one-page overview of the program and key messages that volunteers can use when talking to residents? I can help draft that if we agree it belongs in A5.

Good feedback. I can adjust A2 so that for event 1 we aim for 3 activity facilitators, with 2 as the minimum viable number if recruitment falls short. For events 2 and 3, we can keep the baseline at 2 and revisit after the first debrief. I will also add your point, @523420, about this being a stretch target rather than a hard requirement.

On the data helper role, I will update A2 to specify that this should be a staff member or a returning volunteer who has already done the onboarding in A5. We can highlight this in the training content under T8 so that event leads know who is responsible for the forms and headcounts.

Thanks for the draft, this is very helpful. Before we lock in numbers for D3, I want to check one thing: in A2 you assume that we will have the same number of volunteers for all three events. Given the 21-day window and possible drop-offs, should we plan to recruit a slightly larger pool overall, knowing that not everyone will be available for every date? For example, if we need 7 people on-site for event 1, perhaps we should aim for 10 to 12 active volunteers in total.

I would support building in that buffer. From a scheduling perspective under T11, having 10 to 12 volunteers in the pool gives us more flexibility to cover sickness or last-minute changes, especially since we are not paying overtime. We just need to be clear in A5 that even if someone cannot attend all events, they still go through the same onboarding steps.

That makes sense. I will revise A2 so that our target is 10 to 12 volunteers in the pool, with the understanding that we need at least 7 on-site for event 1 and 6 for events 2 and 3. I will also adjust the recruitment timeline in T2 to reflect that we need to start outreach to internal staff and partners this week.
Happy to help with the one-page overview. If we include it in A5, we can also reuse parts of it for flyers and online posts in T7, so volunteers and residents see consistent messages.

Great, thanks. I will add a placeholder section in A5 for that overview and tag it as content to be drafted with you. For T8, I am currently planning the onboarding flow as: 1) confirmation email with basic info and link to policies, 2) short online or phone briefing, 3) in-person huddle 30 minutes before the event. Does that feel sufficient, or do we need an extra step for safeguarding sign-off?

Given the nature of the pilot and the fact that we are not doing home visits yet, I think your three-step flow is adequate, as long as the online or phone briefing explicitly covers safeguarding, privacy, and escalation routes. We should also ensure that volunteers confirm they have read the key policies. We can add a simple acknowledgement in A5 rather than a complex sign-off process.

From the data side, it would be helpful if the onboarding also includes a short explanation of why we are collecting the three core metrics in A4, and how we protect personal information. That can be a short paragraph in A5 and a slide or handout in T8.

Understood. I will incorporate a short section on data collection purpose and privacy into A5 and the T8 materials. Once I have updated A2 and A5 with all of this feedback, I will share a quick summary here so we can formally confirm the volunteer numbers and onboarding flow.

Quick update: A2 now reflects a target pool of 10 to 12 volunteers, with per-event needs of 1 event lead, 2 welcome desk volunteers, 3 activity facilitators for event 1 (2 minimum), 2 activity facilitators for events 2 and 3, and 1 data helper who is staff or a returning volunteer. A5 now describes the three-step onboarding flow we discussed, including safeguarding, privacy, escalation routes, and a short program overview that @99312 will help draft. Unless there are objections, I suggest we treat these as our agreed numbers and onboarding approach for the pilot.

Thanks for consolidating. I am comfortable with those numbers and the onboarding flow for this pilot. Let us proceed on that basis so that recruitment under T2 and training under T8 can start immediately.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in the design and logistics for the first outreach event.

messages.text: Hi everyone, I have drafted the concept for the first outreach event and a logistics and risk checklist in A7, based on the operating procedures in A3 and the calendar in A6. This covers most of T3 and the first part of T9. The proposal is: a three-hour afternoon event at the Riverside Community Centre, with a welcome area, an information corner for services, a quiet space for older adults, and a small activity corner for children. I have pencilled in two possible dates in A6, both within the 21-day window. Please review A7 and share thoughts on the date, time, and whether the run-of-show feels realistic with the staffing plan from A2.

Thanks for putting this together. Looking at A6 and our overall timeline in T11, both proposed dates are feasible, but the earlier one leaves us only 10 days for recruitment and onboarding. Given the dependencies on T2, T8, and T10, I would lean toward the slightly later date to give us a bit more breathing room while still staying within the 21 days.

From the recruitment side, I agree with @523420. The later date in A6 gives us a more realistic window to confirm 10 to 12 volunteers under T2 and run the onboarding steps in A5. If we go with the earlier date, we might end up with fewer trained volunteers on-site, which would increase pressure on staff.

For data collection in T10, the later date also helps us test the tools in a dry run beforehand, as required in the definition of done. We can use A7 to make sure the data capture steps are clearly placed in the run-of-show, for example at the entrance and near the exit.

On the concept, the three-hour afternoon slot at Riverside Community Centre works well for communications planning in A6 and T7. It is a familiar venue for residents, and the time is friendly for both older adults and families. I would just suggest we avoid overlapping with the local market day, which I think is on Thursdays. The later date you proposed is a Tuesday, so that should be fine.

I have reviewed A7 and the two date options in A6. Given the dependencies others have mentioned, I also favour the later Tuesday date, with a 2pm to 5pm slot. It balances accessibility for our target groups with enough preparation time. Before we confirm D5, can you confirm that the venue is available and that we can secure basic equipment within budget?

I have a provisional hold on Riverside Community Centre for both dates. I will call them this afternoon to confirm the later Tuesday slot from 2pm to 5pm and check that we can use their chairs, tables, and projector at no extra cost. If there is any issue with equipment, we might need to borrow from another department, which I will coordinate with @523420.

If the venue cannot provide a projector, I can check with facilities and IT about borrowing one, and we can add that to the logistics section of A7 and the event checklist in A3. Just flag it once you have spoken to the centre.

On the run-of-show in A7, I have structured it as: 30 minutes set-up, 15 minutes soft opening, 2 hours main activities, 15 minutes closing announcements, and 30 minutes pack-down. With the staffing plan from A2, I think this is manageable, but I am open to suggestions if we need more time for the welcome or closing parts.

The structure looks good. I would just suggest we extend the soft opening to 30 minutes, so volunteers have more time to get comfortable greeting people and explaining the event. We can slightly shorten the main activities block if needed. I will make sure the onboarding in A5 and T8 includes a short practice for the welcome script.

For data capture, it would help if we schedule a 5-minute pause near the end of the main activities where the data helper checks attendance numbers and collects any remaining feedback forms. We can note that explicitly in A7 so it does not get lost in the flow.

If we extend the soft opening, that also gives us a better window for photos and short quotes for communications, as long as we follow privacy rules. I will align the promotion timeline in A6 and T7 with the confirmed date and time once we lock them in.

I can adjust A7 so that we have 30 minutes soft opening, slightly shorter main activities, and a 5-minute data check near the end as @393987 suggested. That should still fit within the 3-hour slot. I will also highlight the data helper tasks more clearly in the checklist.

Update on the venue: Riverside Community Centre has confirmed availability for the later Tuesday from 2pm to 5pm, and they can provide chairs, tables, and a projector at no extra cost. I have updated A6 and A7 accordingly. Unless there are objections, I suggest we confirm this as the final date, time, and location for event 1.

Thanks for confirming. I am happy to lock in Riverside Community Centre on that Tuesday from 2pm to 5pm as our final choice for event 1. Please proceed with any bookings and internal notifications needed.

On the run-of-show and staffing: with the updated structure in A7 and the volunteer plan in A2, I am comfortable approving the proposed minimum staffing for event 1: 1 event lead, 2 welcome desk volunteers, 3 activity facilitators (2 minimum), and 1 data helper. This should be our baseline for D6, with flexibility to add more helpers if recruitment goes well.

I will reflect the confirmed date, time, location, and staffing baseline in the overall timeline under T11 and in the internal briefing for T12, so that leadership and support teams know what to expect for event 1.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on monitoring, evaluation, and data collection processes.

messages.text: Hi all, I have uploaded a draft Monitoring and Evaluation Framework in A4, which builds on the charter in A1 and covers most of T5. It lists proposed indicators, data sources, and collection frequency for the pilot, focusing on the three core metrics we agreed in TH1. I have also outlined a simple data collection process that we can implement through T10. Please review A4 and share any concerns about feasibility, especially around who collects what, and how often.

Thanks for pulling this together. The three core indicators in A4 look aligned with what we discussed: total unique attendees, share from target neighbourhoods, and proportion finding the event helpful or very helpful. Before we confirm D7, I want to check whether the proposed collection frequency feels realistic. You suggest collecting data at every event and doing a quick review within 48 hours. Is that manageable for the team, given other tasks?

From a coordination perspective under T11, a 48-hour review after each event is tight but doable if we keep it light. We can schedule a short debrief slot in the calendar and use A4 as the template for what we look at: attendance numbers, neighbourhood breakdown, and satisfaction summary. Anything more detailed can wait for the mid-pilot review.

Looking at A4 and A7 together, the data collection steps seem reasonable, but I want to be sure we are not overloading the event lead. In your draft, the event lead is responsible for both running the event and checking the data forms. Could we assign the primary responsibility for data capture to the data helper role we defined in A2, with the event lead just doing a quick final check?

I agree. For T8 and A5, it will be clearer if we say that the data helper is the main person capturing attendance and feedback forms, while the event lead ensures it happens. That way, we can train data helpers more specifically on the forms and storage process.

Good point. I can update A4 so that the data helper is listed as the primary owner for data capture during events, with the event lead as the secondary checker. For T10, I will also specify that the data helper is responsible for uploading the data to the shared location in the knowledge hub, while I handle the aggregation and analysis.

On the tools side, do we already know where the data will live in the knowledge hub index in A8? For example, should we have a dedicated folder for event data, with subfolders per event? That will help us keep things tidy and make it easier to find numbers for communications later.

In the draft A8, I have a section for monitoring and evaluation with subfolders per event. We can align A4 and T10 with that structure: for each event, a folder with scanned or photographed forms and a simple spreadsheet. I will make sure the access rights are set so that only the core team can see raw data.

On indicators, I see in A4 that you have also listed a few optional learning indicators, like number of partner organisations present and number of referrals made. I like having them, but I want to be sure they do not distract from the three core metrics. For D7, I would propose that we confirm the three core indicators as mandatory for every event, and treat the others as nice-to-have if capacity allows.

That works for me. I will mark the three core indicators as mandatory in A4 and clearly label the others as optional learning indicators. For collection frequency, I suggest: core indicators collected at every event, optional ones collected when we have a partner present or when it is easy to do so. We can then summarise both in the mid-pilot review.

From the event side, that split between mandatory and optional indicators is helpful. It means we can focus volunteers on the essentials and only collect extra data when it does not interfere with the flow of the event.

For onboarding in A5 and T8, I will make sure we clearly explain the data helper role and the difference between mandatory and optional indicators, so volunteers know what is expected of them at a minimum.

On responsibilities for D8, my suggestion is: during each event, the data helper is responsible for collecting attendance and feedback forms and placing them in the event folder; the event lead checks that this has been done before leaving; after the event, I will compile the data into the central spreadsheet in A4 and share a short summary in Slack within 48 hours. Does that division of roles work for everyone?
That division sounds clear to me. I will reflect it in the SOPs in A3 and the event checklist in A7, so that it is visible alongside other operational tasks.

To summarise and close decisions here: we will use the three core indicators in A4 as mandatory for every event, with data collected at each event and a light review within 48 hours. Optional learning indicators will be collected when feasible. For responsibilities, the data helper is the primary owner for data capture and upload, the event lead checks completion, and the statistician compiles and shares summaries. I am comfortable confirming this as our monitoring and data collection approach for the pilot.
Thanks, I will finalise A4 accordingly and start preparing the simple data collection tools and dry run for T10, so we are ready before the first event.

threads.thread_goal: Set up operational processes, knowledge hub, and overall timeline.

messages.text: Hi team, I have shared a draft of the Outreach Events Operating Procedures in A3 and the Knowledge Hub Index in A8. These cover most of T4, T6, and T11. A3 includes standard steps and checklists for before, during, and after events, while A8 outlines the folder structure and access rules for our central information hub. I have also sketched a high-level timeline for the 21-day pilot, including key milestones for T1 to T10. Please review and let me know if the processes feel practical and if the hub structure in A8 will work for you day to day.

Thanks for drafting these. Looking at A3, the pre-event checklist is quite detailed, which is good, but I wonder if it might be a bit long for volunteers to follow on the day. Could we split it into a short version for volunteers and a full version for staff, so that volunteers see only the items they are responsible for?

I like that idea. For T8 and A5, it will be easier to train volunteers if we can point them to a concise checklist that matches their tasks. We can keep the full A3 version for staff and event leads, and maybe include a one-page volunteer checklist in A5.

Good suggestion. I can keep A3 as the master SOP and create a shorter volunteer-facing checklist that we link from A5 and A7. That way, we do not lose detail, but volunteers have a simpler view. I will also highlight in A3 which steps are staff-only.

On the knowledge hub in A8, I see you have top-level folders for charter, staffing, events, monitoring, and communications. For T4 and T7, could we also add a simple 'How to use this hub' note that explains where to find the latest versions and who to contact if something is missing? That might help new volunteers and staff who join mid-pilot.
Yes, that is part of T4. I will add a short usage guide into A8 and then share a summary in this channel once it is ready, so everyone knows where to look for A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, and A7.

On the timeline in T11, I appreciate that you have included a slot for testing data collection tools before the first event. Could we also add a brief mid-pilot review after the second event, where we look at the A4 indicators and decide if we need to adjust anything for event 3?

I support adding a mid-pilot review. It aligns with our overall approach and gives us a formal moment to check participation and satisfaction trends. We can also use it to decide whether to adjust messaging in A6 and T7 or staffing for the third event.
I will add a mid-pilot review milestone to T11, scheduled a few days after the second event, and reference A4 as the main input. That will also feed into the internal briefing under T12.

On access rules in A8, I see that volunteers will have read-only access to a 'Volunteers' folder with A5 and the short checklists, while the core team has broader access. That seems appropriate from a confidentiality perspective. Could we also make sure that any documents with personal data, like raw feedback forms, are stored only in restricted folders?

Yes, that is the plan. In A8, I will mark the event data folders as restricted to the core team only, and we will store only aggregated numbers in any documents that volunteers can see. This should help us stay aligned with privacy requirements.

On the during-event checklist in A3, could we add a simple step reminding the event lead to check in with volunteers halfway through, to see if anyone needs a break or support? It is a small thing, but it can make a big difference for how the event feels for the team.
Good call. I will add a mid-event check-in step to A3 and the event checklist in A7, so it becomes part of the standard routine.

Once the usage guide in A8 is ready, I can help turn it into a short message for this channel and a simple visual if needed, so people can quickly see where to find A1 to A7 and the event calendar in A6.

I have now updated A3 with the staff and volunteer checklists, the mid-event check-in, and references to data responsibilities. A8 includes the final folder structure, access rules, and a short usage guide. The timeline in T11 shows key milestones: charter finalisation, staffing and onboarding, event 1, mid-pilot review, events 2 and 3, and the internal briefing under T12. I propose that we confirm this hub structure and timeline so that everyone can start using them immediately.

Thanks for the thorough work. I am happy to confirm the knowledge hub structure and access rules in A8, as well as the project timeline and milestones in T11, as our baseline for the pilot. Please proceed with sharing the usage guide in this channel and preparing the internal briefing under T12.
